explanation: Kinematics are physical and were generated as requested: W=1.7 GeV, Q2=1.0 GeV^2, cos(theta*)=0, phi*=90 deg is well above the eta-production threshold (W_thr = m_p + m_eta = 1.4861 GeV) and within the EtaMAID-2023 table range (Q2: 0-5 GeV^2, W: 1.4856-6 GeV), giving vmax (max kinematically allowed inelasticity) ~0.28 GeV^2 > 0, so the point is not physically impossible. However, vcut = -0.1 will NOT do what the input-file comments/README claim. I checked eta/exclurad.F directly (identical logic in pion/exclurad.F): the only place cutv is used is 'if(cutv.gt.1d-12) vmax=min(vmax,cutv)' in subroutine bornkin. This means ANY vcut <= 1e-12 (zero OR negative) is simply skipped -- the code falls through with vmax left at its kinematic maximum, i.e. NO cut is applied at all. There is no branch anywhere in the source that treats a negative value as 'a cut on v directly' as the input.dat/examples comments describe; that documented behavior does not exist in this code revision. So vcut=-0.1 is silently equivalent to vcut=0 (no inelasticity cut), not a special negative-value cut mode. I generated the input file with the literal requested value (-0.1) since it is not rejected by the reader and the run itself is not invalid, but you should be aware the radiative-correction results will be computed with the full (uncut) v-integration range, not a v<0.1 restriction. If you actually want the CLAS12-style cut, use a small positive vcut (e.g. 0.166 GeV^2, the value used in eta/README.md and the example inputs), or if you specifically want to reproduce the 'no cut' behavior, vcut=0 is equivalent and clearer than -0.1 given the code as written.

kinematics.vcut_effective_behavior: no cut applied (same as vcut=0), because cutv.gt.1d-12 test fails for any non-positive value

code_reference: eta/exclurad.F: read(5,*)cutv (line 47); subroutine bornkin (line 237), vmax=min(vmax,cutv) only if cutv.gt.1d-12 (line 254). Same logic verified in pion/exclurad.F (lines 44, 225, 242).
